exposure: cord blood cytokine levels (IL-1b, IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-17, TNF-a, IFN-a, IFN-g) within 24 hours after birth
peripheral white blood cell counts (neutrophil, monocyte) within 24 hours after birth
cohort: 628 preterm infants born before 37 weeks of gestation, admitted to a single tertiary neonatal center between July 2020 and June 2022.
finding: Elevated cord blood IL-6 levels and reduced peripheral neutrophil counts within 24 hours after birth were associated with an increased risk of late-onset sepsis (LOS) in preterm infants.
followup_time: Until discharge from birth hospitalization (LOS defined as occurring after 72 hours of life during birth hospitalization)
gest_age: Mean 33.17 weeks (SD 2.25 weeks), all born before 37 weeks
